status: qualified private Linux export; no publication or device installation
scope: G07/G13: original base gz19h area-1 alarm late registration and this admitted native continuation across guest absence; not full prison-route acceptance.
problem: The original one-shot For(Heroes) registration omits later co-op arrivals. Their refreshed Heroes membership cannot activate area 1, because the native per-character wait was never created. Loading while a guest is absent can also erase the actor behind a pending continuation.
implementation: Before the existing #230/#235 adaptation, admit only the exact canonical AST of 23 original definitions: area #415, registration #416, all 19 #417/alarm/pursuit/reset descendants, and reinforcement loading #180/#181; also require the original WorldScript registration call. Non-original campaigns, other maps, changed or missing definitions and LMP do not get the live registrar.

Add one parameterless persistent registration definition. Existing native #417 spawns record stable seen-character keys. While #416 still owns a pending For cursor, the registrar waits. Thereafter only an unseen living visible party actor receives the unmodified #417. No competing guard loop or native body/instruction index is added or changed by this registrar.

Keep already-spent registration keys through save/reload/reconnect; do not suppress the native reset calls back to #417. Original Sleep(20) is 20 native ticks = 1.1 seconds; original reset Sleep(1) is one native tick = 0.055 seconds.

For this source-admitted family only, retain raw stable hero references as runtime metadata. Missing actors hold existing native frames and remaining poll/Sleep. Save writes the retained reference back into the original serialized this field, so another absent save/reload still has identity. Generic _deser is unchanged.

Preserve a saved unresolved Try1 reference. Resolve it when its hero returns only while the live global remains null. A newly queued #48 does not discard it: the later original Try1 assignment wins when its body actually runs.

On a marked co-op-to-solo snapshot, explicitly project the shared registrar seen keys; native actor continuations continue through existing CoopVmState projection. The watcher has no host-bound parameter that could cause it to be discarded. Only recipient and retained named host-role identities survive; nonhero keys are retained.

Old saves recover only when an actual native registration/wait/pursuit/reset instance proves the family is active. Pending killed+nonempty-frame waits count as anchors. Seen identity can come from a retained raw reference when the actor is absent. No-history old saves are not guessed or rearmed.

limits: Integration uses actual original map startup, actual Session hero creation and local protocol-13 ENet, but actor positions are controlled, AI/combat paused and VM ticks bounded explicitly. No full prison/captive/Nalo/Jun/Shaina route, guard pathfinding/combat, rendered acceptance, Windows, internet/WAN or timing/FPS claim.

State fixture uses prepared actor/guard doubles and synthetic serialized edge rows around original definitions. Its native For, dispatch, reset and Sleep instructions execute; its mocked guards are not proof of real reinforcement admission. The separate ENet startup control demonstrates original AddMob and orders on all eight authored guards.

The old host-side save with an idle protagonist #417 is recoverable while loading on the host. If solo projection of a pre-fix save removes that sole host-owned anchor, no guest history is invented; that ambiguity stays a documented limitation.
Raw saved references already lost by older saves cannot be reconstructed without remaining native identity/history.
The copied original assets and real user save archive were not edited. Every run used an isolated disposable profile. No build installed or published.

Every retained functional run has one startup screen-space-AA warning from headless Compatibility; no script/runtime error is counted as accepted. Other-process inventories are in each run.json and some runs saw an unrelated Godot process; elapsed run durations are logistics only, not performance evidence.

The stated m/u and retained named-role seen-key mapping follows the source implementation; the 70-check state run directly exercises recipient and host removal with actual pending/spent projection, not an additional named-role-key fixture.

The two final 75-check network runs use real ENet, Session loads and original WorldScript/reinforcement MOBs, with prepared positions, frozen unrelated AI and a controlled native VM clock. They are not complete physical prison playthroughs.
The 70 state checks include deliberately constructed serialized edge states; the two original-startup network controls establish actual late-join reachability separately.

Existing regression fixtures contribute 111 checks: captivity 30, base projection 36, LiA projection 21, and actual ENet/solo delayed trap 24. Their scope is retained; the dormant editor trap is a persistence control, not an asserted normal-route trigger.

The state candidate recorded a foreign rendered Godot process at both boundaries; this is functional acceptance only, with no timing comparison. The final network and regression runs retain their own process inventories.
No graphics or native binary change occurred. Prior cloud/terrain/settings acceptance is inherited, not rerun. No new performance, Windows/WAN, Android or full-chapter claim.
Protocol 13, save schema and source version remain unchanged. Original assets and the supplied user saves are untouched.
